models_evaluated: NWL Integrated Care Board hypertension case-finding ML model

links.outcome: Model sensitivity and specificity across demographic and deprivation subgroups
links.effect: Sensitivity higher in older adults and Black patients; specificity higher in younger adults, female and White patients. Higher deprivation had higher sensitivity but lower specificity. Overall sensitivity 62.7%, specificity 60.7%.
links.quote: Sensitivity was higher in older adults and Black patients; specificity was higher in younger adults, female patients, and White patients.

links.outcome: Performance of the ML model versus a more interpretable logistic regression model
links.effect: The ML model's performance was comparable with a more interpretable logistic regression model, so no gain from added complexity.
links.quote: The model's performance was comparable with a more interpretable logistic regression model.

unlisted_practices: Selecting parsimonious, transparent models over complex ones when performance is equivalent

screen.reason: Evaluates an NHS-commissioned predictive model for undiagnosed hypertension prior to/in preparation for deployment, specifically testing performance across sociodemographic subgroups to audit for bias and comparing it to interpretable alternatives.

primary.practice: independent pre-deployment equity and performance auditing
